title: The West Is Sending Russia the Wrong Signals
gist: Gioe argues Europe's fear of vertical escalation lets Putin escalate horizontally via a growing sabotage campaign (100+ attacks, rising) against defense firms and infrastructure; he urges pre-announced, linked costs such as Germany sending Taurus missiles and a claims fund paid from the 200 billion euros of frozen Russian assets at Euroclear.

insights.claim: European leaders conceive of escalation as vertical and immediate, while Moscow escalates horizontally and incrementally below the threshold of conventional war, salami-slicing European security.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Explains why sabotage risk to European infrastructure keeps rising without triggering a decisive response.
insights.quote: But this conception of escalation is largely vertical and immediate, while Moscow is escalating horizontally and incrementally.

insights.claim: Estimates put Russian sabotage across Europe at over a hundred attacks, including potentially devastating ones in Germany in August 2026, and the trajectory is increasing.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Rising physical-security risk to European infrastructure, logistics, and defense assets.

insights.claim: Putin's gray-zone campaign aims to separate Kyiv from its backers by persuading European publics that Ukraine is not worth risking their own security.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Public fatigue is the target; watch European political support for Ukraine aid.

insights.claim: The accretion of sub-threshold attacks may eventually cross a threshold that triggers more aggressive NATO collective defense, as Putin has miscalculated adversaries' resolve before.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Tail risk of a sudden shift to harder NATO-Russia confrontation.
insights.quote: The accretion of sub-threshold attacks may, when added together, end up crossing a threshold for more aggressive collective defense.

insights.claim: Western mixed messages framed as balance or strategic ambiguity in aggregate signal weakness and invite further escalation, leaving Europe deterred by its own fears.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Challenges the consensus that restraint lowers risk; implies more escalation ahead absent policy change.
insights.quote: In aggregate, these vacillations signal weakness.

insights.claim: Russian-linked sabotage increasingly targets defense firms supplying Ukraine, including an August arson at Estonia's Milrem Robotics, a thwarted attack on a Slovak drone facility, and confirmed sabotage at a Polish drone-component factory.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Physical security and insurance costs rise for European drone and defense manufacturers.

insights.claim: Incendiary devices were thrown at the Munich headquarters of Rohde and Schwarz and drone maker Helsing, with two Bulgarian nationals arrested, though Russian sponsorship is unproven.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: High-profile European defense-tech firms face direct sabotage risk.
insights.locator: In Poland, Prime Minister Donald Tusk

insights.claim: Danish intelligence warned Russia is recruiting Danes to prepare sabotage against defense companies supporting Ukraine, and Romanian intelligence disrupted a Russian-coordinated operation targeting military sites.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Sabotage campaign is broadening geographically across NATO.
insights.locator: In Poland, Prime Minister Donald Tusk

insights.claim: Germany narrowly escaped a potential plane crash in July 2024 when a DHL parcel incendiary device ignited at Leipzig airport, and in 2026 there were attempted drone attacks at the same airport against a Ukrainian cargo plane.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Air cargo and logistics networks are exposed to state-backed sabotage.

insights.claim: Germany's response to the 2026 Leipzig plot (closing a consulate and cultural center, expelling diplomats, visa tightening) was desultory and unlikely to cost the Kremlin sleep.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: German rhetoric outpaces action; deterrence credibility remains low.
insights.quote: No one in the Kremlin is likely to have lost any sleep over this.
insights.locator: But after Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt

insights.claim: CIA Director John Ratcliffe warned Russian intelligence against attacking NATO on Aug. 25 without public consequences, and the message was undercut days later by Witkoff and Kushner's cordial Kremlin visit.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: U.S. signaling toward Moscow is inconsistent, reducing deterrence.
insights.locator: Yet despite all this, the response

insights.claim: Trump promised Zelensky at the July 8 NATO summit in Ankara a license for Ukraine to manufacture Patriot interceptors, then reversed weeks later, illustrating a reversal pattern Putin can simply wait out.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: U.S. arms commitments to Ukraine are unreliable; affects defense supply planning.
insights.quote: All Putin needs to do is wait a moment for Trump to perform one of his almost inevitable reversals.

insights.claim: European governments remain hesitant partly because they are still struggling to wean themselves off Russian oil and gas.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Energy dependence constrains European policy toward Russia.

insights.claim: The author proposes Merz provide Ukraine with Taurus cruise missiles explicitly linked to the Leipzig attacks, calling the Taurus debate the acid test of German resolve.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: A Taurus decision would be a major signal of German escalation willingness and defense spending direction.
insights.quote: the debate over providing Ukraine with Taurus cruise missiles has become the acid test of German resolve

insights.claim: Instead of confiscating the 200 billion euros of immobilized Russian sovereign assets at Euroclear at once, the EU could create a claims mechanism paying adjudicated Ukrainian and European sabotage damages from the frozen funds.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: A metered drawdown of frozen assets is a plausible policy path affecting Euroclear and Russian sovereign claims.
insights.quote: Every act of Russian destruction, in Ukraine or in Europe, would then write its own invoice payable from Moscow’s frozen account.

insights.claim: The U.S. could impose costs on Russia across domains: third-country sanctions, more muscular action against the shadow fleet, cyberattacks on Russian intelligence infrastructure, and pressure on Russian extractive operations in Africa.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Shadow fleet enforcement would affect Russian oil export flows and tanker markets.

insights.claim: Effective deterrence requires pre-communicated, specific costs rather than maximum force, because real red lines are usually identified only in hindsight.
insights.speaker: David V. Gioe
insights.so_what: Frames what policy shift would actually change Russian behavior.
insights.quote: Real red lines are usually identified only in hindsight.
